nodes.name: Ru nanoparticles anchored on a nitrogenated holey 2D carbon structure

nodes.source_text: Baek and coworkers obtained low overpotential of 17 mV to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², which were lower than those of Pt/C in 1.0 M KOH solution obtained via Ru nanoparticles anchored on a nitrogenated holey 2D carbon structure (Ru@C2N). Moreover, the turnover frequency (TOF) values of Ru@C2N (0.76 H₂ s⁻¹ at 25 mV; 1.66 H₂ s⁻¹ at 50 mV) were also higher than those of Pt/C (~0.47 H₂ s⁻¹ at 25 mV; 0.95 H₂ s⁻¹ at 50 mV).
the turnover frequency (TOF) values of Ru@C2N (0.76 H₂ s⁻¹ at 25 mV; 1.66 H₂ s⁻¹ at 50 mV) were also higher than those of Pt/C (~0.47 H₂ s⁻¹ at 25 mV; 0.95 H₂ s⁻¹ at 50 mV).
The overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² reduced to ∼100 mV on Li⁺-Ni(OH)₂/Pt islands/Pt(110), which is lower than that on bare Pt(110).
which is lower than that on bare Pt(110).
The obtained Pt3Ni3 nanowires/C-air catalyst yielded current densities of 39.7 (1 M KOH electrolyte) mA cm⁻² at overpotential of 0.07 V
and 23.0 (0.1 M KOH electrolyte) mA cm⁻² at overpotential of 0.07 V, respectively.
the obtained heterostructure delivered a current density of 37.2 mA cm⁻² at overpotential of 70 mV
Qiao and coworkers reported anomalous Ru/C3N4/C catalysts that exhibited small overpotential of 79 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru@CN-0.16 exhibits well-dispersed Ru nanoparticles with particle size of 2.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru@CN-0.16 exhibited well-dispersed Ru nanoparticles (2.3 nm), the highest specific surface area value (632 m² g⁻¹), and the highest percentage of Ru⁰ (70%).
